page: Microsoft Azure E16-8s_v6 is a memory-optimized virtual machine belonging to the Esv6 server family. It is powered by an Intel Xeon 8573C processor utilizing the x86_64 architecture. The server features 8 dedicated vCPUs mapped to 4 physical cores with 2 threads per core, running at a clock speed of 4.2 GHz. It is equipped with 128.0 GB of system memory, yielding a high resource density of 16.0 GB of RAM per vCPU. No local storage is bundled with this instance, though it is Premium Storage capable, and it does not include any GPUs.

Performance benchmarks indicate solid capabilities across standard workloads. The processor supports advanced instruction sets including AVX-512 and Intel AMX (Advanced Matrix Extensions) for deep learning and cryptography. In testing, the server achieved a Geekbench single-core score of 1975.0 and a multi-core score of 7558.0, both falling in the average tier. Text processing performance is a notable strength, scoring 2658.0 in Geekbench (top 25%). However, the Passmark memory score of 1436.15 is relatively weak, and uncached large-block memory read bandwidth sits at 42.29 GB/sec. For lightweight AI tasks, the server achieves a strong text generation speed of 302.13 tokens/sec with a small 135M LLM, but drops to a weak 8.06 tokens/sec on a medium 7B model.

From a cost-efficiency perspective, the E16-8s_v6 offers a high memory-to-vCPU ratio, making it a viable option for memory-intensive workloads that do not require massive parallel compute scaling. The dedicated CPU allocation and large L3 cache of 260 MB support consistent execution. This server is well-suited for memory-heavy applications such as relational databases, in-memory caching layers like Redis (which benchmarked at 11.31 million SET operations per second), enterprise applications, and moderate data processing tasks.
